text:
Montreal arrives at Chicago three days after a 4-3 overtime loss to San Jose, a game the Canadiens let slip after leading by two. They are 3-1-1 in their last five but are without Nick Suzuki, Florian Xhekaj and Ivan Demidov, and Cole Caufield is next in line for Suzuki's minutes. The Blackhawks have had six days to think about a 4-0 loss to Dallas, where Jake Oettinger stopped all 19 shots. They are 2-3-0 in their last five and are missing Andrew Mangiapane, though Bowen Byram could return. Ian Cole also plays his 1,000th NHL game.

The Canadiens have controlled more of the play. At five on five, they have taken 54% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) in their games, against 41% for Chicago. The catch is penalties: Montreal takes 5.4 a game, which keeps handing out power plays. In goal, projected starters Jakub Dobes (MTL) and Spencer Knight (CHI) both sit below expected this season, at -5.7 and -0.7 goals saved above expected. Last year both were well above it, Dobes at +17.3 and Knight at +11.1.

Caufield (41% to score) and Slafkovský lead Montreal's power play. For Chicago, Connor Bedard is 37% to score and 73% for a point, and Patrick Kane is flagged as due. Ice Sheet's under-the-radar pick is Roman Kantserov, 57% for a point tonight, well above his season pace of 35%, because his line creates chances (4.06 expected goals per 60 with him on the ice).
